doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Recording 'Concerto for Doubles' at Carnegie Hall
summary: A 50-piece midnight session; the producers absconded with the money and the master.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: That’s right and they were scratchy. But some 78s were not as scratchy as others. My original recording of “Concerto for Doubles,” I’m glad I’m thinking of this, we had a 50 piece orchestra. Manor. M-A-N-O-R. They were on 57th Street just west of Broadway or Eighth Avenue. Sam Lyra and his partner. Ralph Herman was arranging for the company for different singers, and Ralph said, “Why don’t we do something different? Al Gallodoro just performed a ‘Concerto for Doubles’ that Paul Whiteman had written for him. Why don’t we do this?” and a few other things, the “Fantasy Impromptu.” Do you have that album by the way?

You have it. Well we hired a 50 piece orchestra. We each put up $1,350. The session started right in Carnegie Hall at midnight. And we went until six in the morning. And I did the whole three movements of the “Concerto for Doubles.” Alto sax, bass clarinet, clarinet. Then I did “Oodles of Noodles” and the “Fantasy Impromptu.” But I was in my prime then. 50 piece orchestra. My brother Frank was in the band. And I went to the office one day and he gave me a check for about $240. He says, “I’m going to send Ralph his money” because Ralph went back to Milwaukee. That’s where he was from, Milwaukee, Wisconsin. But Ralph never received any money. They were scoundrels, I’ll tell you right now. They absconded with the money. They absconded with the original platter. Ralph could never get it back. Sam, Irving Berman was the other fellow. He was on the Unfair List for about two or three years in the New York Union newspaper. Unfair List. So that’s the story on the “Concerto for Doubles.” Well those records were a little scratchy. Now I have that in my “Many Sides.” Do you have that? “The Many Sides of Al Gallodoro?”
